title: Complete recipe program with linear material registers and an independently fixed final inventory
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED, NOT SELECTED: read complete passages as executable material-handling programs whose written operands address independently identified containers and material portions. A fixed operation semantics predicts the whole final inventory, not merely a likely action name. IDEA000080 already proposes consumable-carrier replenishment; this is an explicit architectural extension, not a claim that resource consumption is new. GDT446 separates identity from execution context and GDT700 proposes an action-output carry, but neither supplies an independently observed complete material ledger. No source grammar, calibrated inventory, independent operand binding or historically evidenced serialization is currently fixed. No target, control or image was read for this proposal.

design.mechanism: A finite typed instruction alphabet contains TRANSFER, SPLIT, COMBINE, HEAT, COOL and DISCARD. An externally frozen historical recipe grammar must license every instruction and its material-state transition; these English labels are proposed semantics, not inherited Voynich glosses. Each instruction consumes live input-state registers and creates fresh output-state registers. SPLIT and COMBINE conserve a fixed rational material-quantity vector; DISCARD records the residue explicitly. HEAT and COOL preserve material identity while updating a separately fixed state field. Inputs, losses and replenishment may never be silently inserted. A concrete finite serialization is one instruction per complete group: opcode followed by canonical decimal register addresses and rational arguments with fixed separators, all mapped through one global injective symbol key. Every written symbol and every group must be accounted for. The decimal serialization is a falsifiable design assumption, not an attested historical fact.
design.unit: An entire passage is one terminating multi-register program; its initial and final inventories refer to independently bound material portions and containers. Registers use creation order rather than free named-word values. Quantities require an independently calibrated unit; pictorial size alone supplies no amount.
design.contrast: The added constraint over IDEA000080, GDT446 and GDT700 is simultaneous conservation, register lifetime and material provenance over the whole execution, followed by an independent terminal-state prediction. GDT893's source-word bijection neither forces these execution identities nor predicts physical outcomes. Internal type checking alone would remain a structural result under the GDT395 identifiability warning.
design.prediction: Freeze initial inventory, the complete instruction grammar, global symbol key and picture-operand binding without using an independent final scene. All surviving decoders must predict the same complete final inventory and independently measurable state relations. A consumed register reused without explicit production, a negative amount, an unaccounted material output, or disagreement with that final scene refutes the corresponding complete program. No successful fragment, added operation, new object name or local exception rescues it. Selection becomes worthwhile only if a real historical instruction grammar and an independently owned initial/final inventory pair exist.
design.scope: Potential complete operational reading, not recovery of unique historical wording or plant names. CoReMA and ALIM medical source availability audited in GDT893 motivates a source-only search for explicit operations; it does not establish this register notation or supply its parser. Missing calibration, image ownership and independent state observations currently prevent semantic selection. Resource-preserving opcode symmetries must remain unresolved unless an external outcome distinguishes them. This proposal does not reopen geometric proximity ownership or prior action-gloss routes.
